answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post bids, with the stake slashable when a challenge proves the agent double-spent a task or broke a commitment. This does not make identities unique; it makes flooding the market costly. An attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every Sybil, then risk losing it, while honest agents can reuse reputation and stake across jobs. A small delta in stake per identity therefore raises the cost of a large fake-agent garden, even if some attackers still wander in.
